Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

# Quizzy — design notes

## What this release is

Moderator-side quiz preparation plus a playable preview. No player-facing live
game yet (no join codes, no big-screen stage, no websockets/sse).

## Architecture

- `tiny_http` (sync, thread-per-request pool) — no async runtime, fast builds.
- `rusqlite` on the system SQLite — one connection per request,
  `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, `busy_timeout=5000`, WAL journal.
- Hand-rolled: routing, urlencoded form parsing, HTML rendering with escaping,
  Basic auth, base64. See `src/httpd.rs`, `src/routes.rs`, `src/views.rs`, `src/db.rs`.
- Dependencies are vendored in `vendor/` + `.cargo/config.toml`, so
  `cargo build --release --offline` (used by `bin/serve`) needs no network.
- Assets (`assets/quizzy.css`, `assets/Inter-latin.woff2`) are the design's own
  stylesheet/font, embedded in the binary with `include_bytes!` and served at
  `/assets/*`. Small app-specific additions live at the bottom of the css copy.

## Decisions that matter for future steps

- **State**: `quizzes` / `questions` / `options` tables; questions and options
  carry a `position` column; deletes cascade via FK. Question positions can
  have gaps after deletes — moving swaps `position` values with the neighbour.
- **Auth**: everything under `/moderate` (and future moderator routes) requires
  HTTP Basic auth from `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` / `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
  `/up`, `/assets/*` and `/` are public. `SECRET_KEY_BASE` is unused so far
  (reserved for signing player sessions later).
- **Every POST → 303 redirect** (post/redirect/get), except form re-renders on
  validation errors and the preview answer page.
- **"Add option"** is a server roundtrip: the button submits the form with
  `add_option=1`; the server re-renders with one more row and all typed values
  kept, validating nothing. Works without JS.
- **The Active switch** is a real checkbox with `onchange="this.form.submit()"`.
- **Delete confirmations** use native `confirm()` in `onsubmit`.
- **Preview state is in the URL/form** (`n`, `score`) — nothing is persisted,
  per spec. Score is clamped server-side to `0..=active_question_count`.
- **Preview markup reuses the design's `.play-*` (phone) classes**; option
  buttons are real `<button class="play-option">` inside one form, feedback
  uses `.is-revealed` / `.is-correct` / `.is-picked` and
  `.play-status--right/--wrong`.

## QA-facing contract (keep stable)

- Exact labels: "New quiz", "Title", "Save quiz", "Settings", "Delete quiz",
  "Add question", "Question", "Option N" (placeholder+aria-label),
  "Option N is correct", "Active", "Save question", "Add option",
  "Move up", "Move down", "Edit", "Delete", "Preview", "Question X of Y",
  "Correct!", "Wrong!", "Next question", "See score", "Score: X/Y", "Start over".
- Quizzes list: `ul.quiz-list > li.card.quiz-tile`; questions:
  `ol.question-list > li.card.question-item` with all controls inside the `li`.
- Error texts: "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct".

## Testing

- curl smoke tests for auth/CRUD/validation/preview.
- `cdp.py`-style headless Chromium run covered: clicking through quiz/question
  creation, add-option roundtrip, validation errors, reordering, the Active
  auto-save switch, native confirm() accept/dismiss, the whole preview loop,
  settings + delete quiz. 50 checks.

## Quiz export / import (sharing between Quizzy instances)

- **Routes**: quiz page links "Export" → `GET /moderate/quizzes/{id}/export`
  (HTML page whose only `<pre class="code-block">` holds the JSON, ready to
  copy). `/moderate` links "Import quiz" → `GET/POST /moderate/import` with a
  "Quiz JSON" textarea (`name="quiz_json"`) and an "Import" button.
- **Format** (`src/transfer.rs`): exactly `title` + `questions[]` with
  `text`/`active`/`options[]` of `text`/`correct` — no ids, no timestamps; it
  is only for moving contents. Questions/options keep stored order. Export
  always writes both booleans; import treats `active` as optional (default
  true) and `correct` as optional (default false). Unknown keys are ignored,
  so exports from newer versions still import.
- **Validation**: import applies the question-form rules per question (text
  required, ≥2 non-blank options, ≥1 correct among them; blank option rows
  are skipped like the form). All errors are collected and shown in the
  `.errors` box with 1-based question numbers ("Question 2: ...").
- **All or nothing**: everything validates before any INSERT, then
  `db::import_quiz` writes quiz + questions + options in one transaction —
  invalid JSON means no quiz and no partial questions.
- **JSON is hand-rolled** (`src/json.rs`): strict RFC 8259 parser (depth-capped
  at 128 against stack exhaustion) + string quoting. Keeps the vendored
  dependency set unchanged so `bin/serve` still builds offline in seconds.
- Import always creates a **new** quiz (same title allowed) and 303-redirects
  to its page.

## Live game release (games, players, answers)

### Model

- `games`: one row per run of a quiz (`quiz_id`, unique 5-char join `code`
  from an unambiguous alphabet, `status` lobby|playing|finished,
  `question_id` + `question_open` for the current step). A quiz can be played
  any number of times; games **skip inactive questions** (flow only walks the
  active list, by `(position, id)`).
- `players`: per game, no account — `name` + random 128-bit `token`. The
  browser remembers the player via cookie `quizzy_player_<CODE>=<token>`
  (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 7 days): reopening the join link continues as the
  same player; re-POSTing the join form never creates a duplicate.
- `answers`: `(player_id, question_id)` primary key + `option_id`; re-picks
  while the question is open are `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` — the
  last pick counts. Counts are always filtered to the game's own players, so
  replays of a quiz stay isolated.

### Routes

- Moderator (Basic auth): `POST /moderate/quizzes/{id}/games` ("Start a
  game"), `GET .../games/{gid}` (big screen), `GET .../games/{gid}/state`
  (live fragment), `POST .../games/{gid}/action` (`action=start|finish|next|
  end`; the state machine ignores actions that don't fit the phase).
- Public: `GET /play/{code}` (join form, or the remembered player's screen,
  or "The quiz is over" once finished — no more joins), `POST .../join`
  ("Your name" + "Join"; blank name re-renders with "Enter your name"),
  `GET .../state` (fragment, cookie-authenticated), `POST .../answer`
  (upserts only while the question is open and only options of the current
  question).
- The join link is `http://{Host}/play/{code}` from the request's Host header
  (any host works); the same full URL is the QR payload and the plain text.

### Liveness (no websockets, no SSE)

- Both screens poll their `state` endpoint once a second and swap `#live`'s
  innerHTML only when the `X-Game-Version` header changes (FNV-1a of the
  fragment — any visible change flips it). Polling self-heals on crowded
  Wi-Fi and keeps tiny_http's thread pool free (no held connections).
- In-page clicks (stage actions, phone options) are fetch POSTs marked
  `X-Quizzy-Live: 1`; those get `204` back and immediately re-pull state, so
  nobody ever reloads. Without JS the same forms do a plain POST → 303 and
  still work end to end.
- **Fetch URLs are resolved against `location.origin`** — never against the
  document base — so the app keeps working when the moderator browses with
  `user:pass@host` in the address bar (Chromium refuses fetch() on URLs with
  embedded credentials).
- The phone fragment for an open question contains no correctness hint at all
  (no class/data attribute); only after "Finish" do phones render
  `is-correct`/"Correct" and the verdict "Correct!" / "Wrong!" / "No answer".

### Rendering

- Big screen reuses the design's `.screen/.lobby/.qr/.counter-pill/
  .stage-*/.answers-counter/.screen-controls`; phones reuse `.play-*` with
  `.play-option__mark` for "Your answer"/"Correct" and `.play-status--*`.
  The counter pill wraps its text in one inline span so `innerText` is
  exactly "Players: 2" (inline-flex would inject a newline before <strong>).
- QR codes are inline SVG generated with the vendored `qrcodegen` crate
  (ECC M), dark modules in the design's night ink; verified against the QR
  finder patterns.

### QA-facing contract (new labels, keep stable)

"Start a game", "Start", "Finish", "Next", "End quiz", "Players: N",
"Question X of Y", "Answers: A / B", "Correct" (option mark), "The quiz is
over", "Your name", "Join", "Hi, <name>!", "Your answer", "Correct!",
"Wrong!", "No answer".
